\olsection{Extensionality}

Two structures that agree on the symbols of a sentence give it the same
truth value. % \begin{defn} in a comment is not an item. \end{defn}

\begin{defn}[Agreement]
\ollabel{defn:agree}
Structures $M_1$ and $M_2$ \emph{agree} on a set of symbols when they have
the same domain and the same interpretation of each symbol in the set.
\end{defn}

\begin{prop}[Extensionality]
\ollabel{prop:extensionality}
If $M_1$ and $M_2$ agree on the symbols of a sentence $A$
(\olref{defn:agree}), then $A$ is true in $M_1$ iff it is true in $M_2$.
\end{prop}

\begin{proof}
By induction on the formation of $A$, with \olref[fol][syn][ext]{prop:extensionality}
for the subformulas. The cost is 100\% routine.
\end{proof}

\begin{rem}
A remark is not an item.
\end{rem}
